before.evidence: Counterexample: $f$ is chosen nonzero, so both restrictions are nonzero; the zero modification would be trivial and is not used.

after.evidence: Counterexample steps 1.1–1.2 require only the prescribed difference G−hat f=1 on the sphere. Nonzero Schwartz f does not force either restriction to be nonzero: for example a nonzero Schwartz transform (|xi|²−1)exp(−|xi|²) vanishes on the sphere. Zero values of either restriction do not affect their everywhere difference or the refutation.

before.evidence: Statement: the extension bound at $q_0$ implies the restriction estimate at $p_0$ by the same duality; sharpness in part (c) is the exact negation at the endpoint.

after.evidence: The endpoint extension bound at q0 implies the endpoint restriction bound at p0 by the supplied duality. Proof step 4.1 invokes the Knapp obstruction only for p>p0 or q<q0; it does not negate the endpoint estimates proved in steps 2.1–3.1.

before.evidence: Statement: the radial integration has the exceptional endpoint $r=1$; the proof shows a single radius contributes zero measure.

after.evidence: Proof steps 1.1–3.1 isolate r=1 as an interior exceptional radius of (0,infinity), not an integration endpoint. It contributes zero because the singleton is Lebesgue null; r=0 is outside the polar domain, and no value at infinity is evaluated.
